data_source_note: Generated from synthetic test data produced by the WSA PCAP generator. Findings describe characteristics of artificial captures and do not reflect any real wireless environment.

findings.title: WEP Encryption Detected
findings.explanation: The AP sets the Privacy capability bit in its beacons but advertises no RSN Information Element. This combination indicates WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy), deprecated since IEEE 802.11i-2004 and cryptographically broken.
findings.impact: WEP keys can be recovered in under 60 seconds with freely available tools given approximately 5 000 captured initialisation vectors. All WEP-protected traffic is effectively transmitted in plaintext.
findings.remediation: Replace WEP immediately with WPA3-Personal (preferred) or WPA2-Personal (AES/CCMP). There is no configuration or firmware change that can make WEP cryptographically secure; hardware that does not support WPA2 must be retired or replaced.
